note: The healthy ruleset with two deliberate plants, one per direction of the leak question. (1) The declared canary se-canary-nft-4f21a9c7d0 sits in a rule COMMENT — free text an operator can put anything into, which nft-chains reads past — and the canary checks assert it reaches no output channel. (2) A synthetic regular chain named se-canary-chain-7e19c4b2d6 pins the opposite truth: chain NAMES are emitted by design, so a credential pasted into one WILL travel — the token is therefore not in `canaries` (it legitimately appears in the expected stream) and is anchored below instead, so a collector that suppressed or rewrote the name fails the anchor. Before the second plant this variant was the healthy payload plus a field nothing reads, and its replay proved nothing healthy's did not.
anchors_note: Staged truth read from the payload by hand: the input-allow anchors match healthy's (the plant does not touch reachability), and the canary chain was created at staging with no hook, no rules and no rule targeting it — so it must be emitted, name intact, as an unreferenced empty chain. nft-tables added 2026-08-23 with the R3d port, over the same staged ruleset: 7 table(s), counted by hand off nft.json's own entries — a table entry opens a row, chains label it, rules count into it.
